Example robot models

Source: R/catalog.R
robot_example.Rd

Returns validated example models. All are serial manipulators built from standard Denavit-Hartenberg parameters, with link frames at the distal end of each link.

robot_example(name = c("planar2", "planar1", "planar3", "puma560", "branched"))

Arguments

name

Model name.

Value

A robot_model.

Details

  • "planar1": one revolute link of length 1 m, a uniform 1 kg rod.

  • "planar2": two revolute links of length 1 m, uniform 1 kg rods, limits \([-\pi, \pi]\). End effector \((\cos q_1 + \cos(q_1 + q_2), \sin q_1 + \sin(q_1 + q_2))\).

  • "planar3": three revolute links of lengths 1, 0.8 and 0.6 m with masses 1, 0.8 and 0.6 kg.

  • "puma560": kinematic model of the PUMA 560 arm using the standard DH parameters and joint limits published with the Robotics Toolbox (Corke, 2017, Robotics, Vision and Control, 2nd ed., Springer). No inertial parameters are included.

  • "branched": a five-link tree with two fingers on a revolute wrist, including a fixed joint, used to demonstrate branched kinematics.

Examples

robot_example("planar2")
#> <robot_model> planar2: 3 links, 2 joints, 2 degrees of freedom
#> end effector: link2
#>    name     type parent child q_index     lower    upper
#>  joint1 revolute   base link1       1 -3.141593 3.141593
#>  joint2 revolute  link1 link2       2 -3.141593 3.141593
robot_example("puma560")
#> <robot_model> puma560: 7 links, 6 joints, 6 degrees of freedom
#> end effector: link6
#>    name     type parent child q_index      lower     upper
#>  joint1 revolute   base link1       1 -2.7925268 2.7925268
#>  joint2 revolute  link1 link2       2 -0.7853982 3.9269908
#>  joint3 revolute  link2 link3       3 -3.9269908 0.7853982
#>  joint4 revolute  link3 link4       4 -1.9198622 2.9670597
#>  joint5 revolute  link4 link5       5 -1.7453293 1.7453293
#>  joint6 revolute  link5 link6       6 -4.6425758 4.6425758
